strategies.title: Diameter-constrained multistart packing
strategies.plan: Start from a 16-point subset of the triangular lattice obtained by taking the radius-two hexagonal cluster and deleting three alternating outer vertices, then normalize its maximum pair distance to one. Introduce a scalar separation variable \(t\), maximize \(t\), and impose smooth inequalities \(\|p_i-p_j\|^2-t^2\ge0\) and \(1-\|p_i-p_j\|^2\ge0\) for every pair; this converts the min/max ratio into constrained optimization. Run deterministic SLSQP multistarts from the normalized lattice seed plus fixed-seed small perturbations, using analytic Jacobians for both pairwise constraint families, and retain only the candidate with the largest exactly recomputed ratio. Translation is removed by centering each start and scale is fixed by diameter normalization, so all returned arrays remain shape `(16,2)` and valid. Expected-gain check: the acceptance rule replaces the lattice fallback only when its exactly evaluated `min_max_ratio` is strictly higher, preserving all score factors and therefore strictly raising `combined_score` over the fallback whenever accepted.

strategies.title: Diameter-pair gauge polishing
strategies.plan: Remove translation, rotation, and scale degeneracy by relabelling a current diameter pair as points 0 and 1, fixing them exactly at `(0,0)` and `(1,0)`, and optimizing only the remaining 14 points plus separation variable `t`. Use smooth constraints `||pi-pj||²-t² >= 0` and `1-||pi-pj||² >= 0` with analytic Jacobians; retain the original multistart result as fallback. Run several deterministic tiny coordinate perturbations in this gauge, accepting only evaluated normalized configurations whose squared ratio improves the incumbent. This is better conditioned than allowing the optimizer to drift in four irrelevant similarity directions while trying to identify the diameter. Expected-gain check: every accepted result is explicitly tested against `0.0775841541474`, hence its predicted `combined_score` is strictly greater than `1.00000280888` (otherwise the valid incumbent fallback is returned).

strategies.title: Central-core boundary surgery
strategies.plan: From the best incumbent, sort points by distance from the centroid and temporarily freeze the six most central points after diameter-gauge normalization. Reoptimize the ten outer points and `t` under the same all-pairs smooth inequalities, then release all 16 points for a final full constrained polish. Repeat this deterministically for central-core sizes 5, 6, and 7 and for both choices among tied diameter pairs. The temporary frozen core changes the active contact graph primarily on the boundary, where a triangular-lattice cluster usually wastes diameter through uneven deleted boundary sites. Every intermediate configuration is checked with all 120 pair constraints, and only normalized improvements replace the incumbent. Expected-gain check: replacement requires a directly evaluated squared ratio above `0.0775841541474`, so any accepted result has predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Threefold annular topology escape
strategies.plan: Create deterministic structural starts with one center point, a radius-`r1` triangle at angles `0, 2π/3, 4π/3`, and two six-point rings at radii `r2,r3` with phases `a,b`, giving exactly `1+3+6+6=16` points. Enumerate `a,b` on multiples of `π/12`, use radii `(0.30,0.58,0.90)`, `(0.35,0.62,0.92)`, and `(0.40,0.66,0.94)`, normalize each, and first optimize the five ring parameters with the auxiliary separation variable. Expand each result to unrestricted 16-point coordinates and perform the all-pairs constrained polish, retaining the best valid result. This explores a contact topology unavailable to small perturbations of the deleted-site triangular cluster while preserving exact cardinality and diameter normalization. Expected-gain check: the final acceptance test requires squared ratio `> 0.0775841541474`, therefore any accepted configuration has predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Delaunay-topology start bank
strategies.plan: Add deterministic non-lattice starts representing several boundary/contact topologies: 9+6+1, 10+5+1, 11+4+1, 12+4 annuli, plus two-ring variants, each with multiple relative phase offsets. Run the existing exact diameter-constrained SLSQP formulation from every start, retaining its auxiliary separation variable `t`, so all final candidates satisfy pairwise `t² <= d_ij² <= 1`. Keep the triangular-lattice, noisy, and greedy starts as fallbacks because they already establish the incumbent basin. This is structurally different from random perturbation because the outer and inner ring cardinalities force different Delaunay graphs before constrained polishing. Expected-gain check: normalize and accept a candidate only when its squared ratio exceeds `0.0775841541474`, equivalently `combined_score > 1.00000280888`; otherwise return the valid incumbent.

strategies.title: Gauge-fixed active-contact polish
strategies.plan: After each successful constrained solve, identify lower contacts with `d_ij²-t² < 1e-7` and diameter contacts with `1-d_ij² < 1e-7`. Remove translation and rotation null directions by fixing one diameter endpoint at the origin and the other on the positive x-axis, then rerun SLSQP with analytic Jacobians from this gauge-fixed representation. The reduced coordinate system eliminates the nearly singular rigid-motion directions present in the current 33-variable formulation and permits tighter convergence of the same hard inequalities. Preserve the original solution whenever the polished result is not feasible after normalization. Expected-gain check: accept only a normalized feasible polish whose squared ratio is strictly above `0.0775841541474`, giving `combined_score > 1.00000280888`, else retain the incumbent.

strategies.title: Rotated seven-point core replacement
strategies.plan: For each incumbent-like solution, select the seven points nearest its centroid and replace them by a rotated, contracted copy about their own centroid: use rotations of 15, 30, and 45 degrees and contraction factors 0.82, 0.88, and 0.94. Keep the other nine points fixed in the initial condition, then release all 16 points into the exact `t² <= d_ij² <= 1` optimization; this changes only the mesoscopic core contact graph while retaining the successful outer hull. Include both rotation signs, normalize every seed, and retain the original solution as fallback. The replacement is deterministic and explores a core-shell rearrangement unavailable to infinitesimal lattice noise. Expected-gain check: return a replacement only after direct normalized evaluation proves squared ratio `> 0.0775841541474`, hence `combined_score > 1.00000280888`; otherwise return the incumbent.
